ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #13
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which conjunction means the same as 'but' in 'The room was small, ____ it was very clean'? (1 mark)
   A. yet
   B. for
   C. nor
   D. so

2. Which is a main idea of the text 'Keeping Clean to Stay Healthy'? (1 mark)
   A. Good hygiene keeps us healthy
   B. Soap is expensive
   C. Germs are good for us
   D. Flies help us

3. Which word is a preposition of position? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. run
   C. under
   D. happy

4. Which sentence is a direct question and needs a question mark at the end? (1 mark)
   A. I like apples
   B. Where is the school
   C. We went home
   D. Please close the door

5. Which is written in block letters? (1 mark)
   A. WANJIKU KAMAU, in capital letters only
   B. wanjiku kamau, in small letters
   C. Wanjiku, in joined writing
   D. Wanjiku Kamau, with capitals at the start of each name

6. A roundabout is (1 mark)
   A. a straight road
   B. a circular junction where vehicles go around in one direction
   C. a railway
   D. a type of bridge

7. Which of these is NOT an adverb? (1 mark)
   A. nearby
   B. early
   C. tidy
   D. slowly

8. 'Steal' means to (1 mark)
   A. take something that does not belong to you
   B. read a book
   C. wash clothes
   D. give a gift

9. To retell a story, which things should you say? (1 mark)
   A. Only the title
   B. Only the last word
   C. The page numbers
   D. Who, where, what happened and how it ended

10. What does it mean to read a poem interpretively? (1 mark)
   A. To think about its meaning and feelings and show them in your voice
   B. To copy it
   C. To read it silently in one second
   D. To count the words

11. In the passage about Mama Neema's farm, why does she call weeds thieves? (1 mark)
   A. They eat the goats
   B. They steal water and food from the maize
   C. They steal tools from the shed
   D. They take the children's lunch

12. Which closing is suitable for a friendly letter? (1 mark)
   A. To whom it may concern,
   B. Yours faithfully,
   C. Yours lovingly,
   D. Dear Sir,

13. Which sentence should end with a full stop, not a question mark? (1 mark)
   A. What is her name
   B. Where is the clinic
   C. Are you ready
   D. She asked where the clinic was.

14. At the end of a statement, the voice usually (1 mark)
   A. falls
   B. rises
   C. hides
   D. shouts

15. Choose the correct pair: '___ tall boy and ___ old woman.' (1 mark)
   A. An, a
   B. An, an
   C. The, an
   D. A, an

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Write an SMS inviting a friend to your birthday party on Saturday at 3 o'clock. (3 marks)

17. Explain the difference between 'my' and 'mine'. Use each in a sentence. (3 marks)

18. Write the missing forms: good, better, ___ ; bad, ___ , worst; many, more, ___ . (3 marks)

19. Name the three parts of a narrative and say what goes in each. (3 marks)

20. List three parts of a diary entry. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #13 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — yet
   'Yet' shows a surprise, like 'but'.

2. A — Good hygiene keeps us healthy
   The whole text supports good hygiene.

3. C — under
   'Under' shows where something is.

4. B — Where is the school
   It is a direct question.

5. A — WANJIKU KAMAU, in capital letters only
   Block letters are capital letters.

6. B — a circular junction where vehicles go around in one direction
   Traffic moves round a central island.

7. C — tidy
   'Tidy' is an adjective.

8. A — take something that does not belong to you
   Stealing is taking what is not yours.

9. D — Who, where, what happened and how it ended
   A retelling covers characters, place, events and ending.

10. A — To think about its meaning and feelings and show them in your voice
   Interpretive reading brings out meaning and feeling.

11. B — They steal water and food from the maize
   The passage says weeds steal water and food from the maize.

12. C — Yours lovingly,
   Yours lovingly is friendly.

13. D — She asked where the clinic was.
   It reports a question, so it is a statement.

14. A — falls
   Statements usually end with a fall.

15. D — A, an
   Tall starts with a consonant sound, old starts with a vowel sound.

SECTION B
----
16. (3 marks)
   Answer: Hi Kamau. Please come to my birthday party on Saturday at 3 o'clock at my home. Thank you. Ann.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for greeting, 1 for day, time and place, 1 for politeness and name.

17. (3 marks)
   Answer: My comes before a noun (This is my bag). Mine stands alone (The bag is mine).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sentence and 1 mark for the difference.

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: best; worse; most
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

19. (3 marks)
   Answer: Beginning: who, where and when. Middle: the events and problem. End: how it is solved and how people felt.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

20. (3 marks)
   Answer: Day and date; greeting (Dear Diary); body (events and feelings); sign-off. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
